top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. Magic-wavelength trapping lets thousands of neutral atoms be held in the Lamb-Dicke regime with equal light shifts on both clock levels, which is a distinct mechanism from the 2005 comb and the 2012 ion-control prizes. The 10^-18 performance has been reproduced across JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE and NIST, and the two roles are separable: Katori for the concept, Ye for accuracy and the many-atom clock. The citation is scoped to the lattice concept and demonstrated 10^-18 performance, not to the redefinition of the second. The remaining weaknesses are the absence of a fundamental-physics result so far and incomplete credit to Ludlow, Lemke, Hinkley, Bloom, Takamoto and Lemonde, but they do not outweigh the maturity of the work. No award is a poorer outcome than this mature, reproduced achievement with clean attribution.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for B013, Katori or Ye; as WACQT director and a Chalmers superconducting-circuits theorist, I would recuse on any proposal centred on circuit QED, which is not in this slate
